finding.claim: POST /settings/email is a state-changing account operation protected by @login_optional instead of @login_required. Unauthenticated requests are not rejected, and set_email is called with g.uid = None. A sibling route (/settings/password) correctly uses @login_required, so this looks like a decorator mix-up. Depending on how set_email is implemented, this can change the email of a null/unowned account or of every row where uid IS NULL. It can also cause a 500 or a silent no-op, and it breaks the authorization invariant.
finding.source: Unauthenticated remote HTTP client sending POST /settings/email with no session cookie.
finding.sink: set_email(g.uid, ...) at routes.py:37, an account email modification. This is the standard account-recovery pivot.

trace.note: login_optional sets g.uid = session.get('uid') (None when unauthenticated) and always calls the wrapped view
@login_optional applied, no 401 abort on a missing session
set_email(g.uid, 'new@example.org') is invoked with uid=None for anonymous callers
set_email is a stub here, so the real impact depends on the implementation. If it keys on uid with None/NULL matching, it is exploitable.

finding.guards_checked: login_required is applied only to /settings/password (routes.py:41-42), not to this route. There is no in-handler check of g.uid, no CSRF protection, no role check, and no before_request hook or middleware. set_email does not validate the uid, since it is a stub. Checked and unchanged: the /feed route is intentionally optional-auth and returns no user data. Caveat: set_email's body is a stub, so exploitability beyond the missing auth gate is unconfirmed. The missing authentication check on the route is confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none (login_optional at routes.py:19-25 only sets g.uid=None and never aborts; no in-handler check, before_request hook or middleware)
verdict.reason: routes.py:34-37 lets an anonymous caller reach set_email(None, ...) through @login_optional, which never aborts (routes.py:22-23), unlike @login_required at routes.py:11-12; the missing auth gate is real, but set_email is a stub (routes.py:48-49), so the impact beyond that can't be shown from this code.
